source_findings: mkosi exposes separate lifecycle verbs: shell/boot use systemd-nspawn; vm uses a configured virtual-machine monitor and defaults to qemu. This makes container and VM fidelity distinct first-class execution lanes rather than one interchangeable backend.

systemd-vmspawn explicitly launches a full virtual machine rather than namespaces. Current source exposes image/directory boot, CPU/RAM controls, KVM and VSOCK capability handling, TPM/swtpm, EFI NVRAM state, Secure Boot selection, raw/qcow2 image handling and multiple virtual disk types.

Current vmspawn source includes an ephemeral image mode that runs from a temporary filesystem snapshot and removes it at termination. This is useful for deterministic clean-slate fault scenarios, but by construction cannot prove persistence unless a persistent-image test lane is used.

mkosi's boot lane exercises systemd inside an nspawn container and is therefore useful for fast package/service/installer regression, but it shares the host kernel and cannot establish guest-kernel, firmware, KVM, TPM, EFI/NVRAM or physical-device fidelity.

mkosi's vm lane can provide a materially stronger pre-physical boot boundary. Its configured VMM may be qemu or vmspawn; hard-coding one VMM would unnecessarily reduce portability and create a moving-tool dependency.

vmspawn has Ubuntu/Debian-specific host prerequisites around KVM/VSOCK group access. These are host capability requirements, not evidence that F2 is correctly installed; the twin must probe and fail closed rather than silently weakening host security settings.

The external tools are actively evolving. Exact mkosi/systemd versions and source identities therefore need to be part of every TwinBackendProfile and receipt; distro-default tool names alone are insufficient provenance.

Neither mkosi nor vmspawn supplies F2-WP-1203's desktop-session, PipeWire/WirePlumber, portal/compositor, browser or real-device fault semantics automatically. A successful VM boot remains lower-fidelity evidence than the complete hostile-target twin and never grants T4 physical credit.

f2_distillation.recommended_shape: Use mkosi as a pinned external image/lifecycle compiler and expose at least two explicit twin lanes: NSPAWN_FAST for low-cost userspace/service regression and VM_BOOT for higher-fidelity guest-kernel/boot/lifecycle tests using a pinned VMM (vmspawn or qemu). Preserve backend capability/fidelity gaps in typed state.
thin_native_rules: Never let NSPAWN_FAST imply guest-kernel or firmware fidelity.
Never let VM_BOOT imply desktop/device or physical-target fidelity.
Pin mkosi/systemd/VMM identities and record host capability probes before granting twin evidence.
Use ephemeral VM snapshots for clean-slate scenarios; use explicit persistent image copies for update/rollback/reboot persistence tests.
Treat KVM/VSOCK/TPM/EFI/NVRAM availability as observed capability fields with UNKNOWN/UNAVAILABLE states, not assumed defaults.
Keep portable image configuration separate from host-trusted privilege policy; an image must not self-grant host capabilities.
Invoke the external CLI/tool boundary instead of coupling F2 to mkosi internals unless a later ablation proves an API-level integration materially superior.

counterhypothesis: A single direct-QEMU or generic container harness may achieve equivalent defect discovery with fewer dependencies; mkosi/vmspawn could add a fast-moving orchestration layer without improving F2 acceptance quality.
next_falsifier: Map WP1202/WP1207 requirements against NSPAWN_FAST, mkosi+vmspawn and mkosi+qemu capability matrices, then run an eventual Trigger-4 ablation on identical install/reboot/update/failure fixtures measuring defect detection, setup determinism, wall time, CPU/RSS/disk I/O and maintenance/configuration surface.
